cover.headline: Initiate at BUY: the online franchise is worth the price; offline is the swing factor
cover.lead: Physicswallah (PW) turned a YouTube physics channel into India's largest test-prep company: 4.87 million students paid for its online courses in FY26 at about ₹4,100 a year, and 0.47 million attended its 353 centres. Revenue grew 35% to ₹3,900 cr in FY26 and 24% in Q1FY27 despite the re-held NEET exam; the online channel earns ~27% margins, the offline network still loses money. At ₹{{P.last|num}} the stock is +13% above the ₹109 IPO price and trades at 28.6x our FY28E EBITDA, against a median one-year-forward multiple of 29.2x since January. Adjusted for the internet platforms' −3.7% move over the same months and rolled forward a year, 28x Sep-28E EBITDA gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with BUY.** Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}} ({{scen.bear.upside|chg}}). The street's median target is ₹139.

arguments.p: ~4.9 million paying students at ~₹4,100 a year, a free YouTube funnel (ads 9% of revenue) and ~27% margins after rent. Online grew 39% in FY26 and 33% in Q1FY27 despite the NEET re-exam.
The network doubled to 366 centres in 15 months and still lost ~10% of revenue after rent in FY26. Mature centres earn 13-15%; management guides break-even in FY27, we assume FY29E.

The stock's own forward EV/EBITDA has a median of 29.2x since January; it trades at 28.6x our FY28E EBITDA. Internet platforms de-rated −3.7% over the same months, so we apply 28x to Sep-28E EBITDA: {{dcf.tp|inr}}; the DCF (₹130) is lower.
Free AI tutors, exam disruptions, a slower offline turnaround and acquisitive capital allocation. Founders own 71%; the float is thin.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): the delayed NEET enrolments should show up; the test is whether H1 revenue growth gets back to ~30%.
Offline break-even: management guides near break-even (after rent) for FY27; Q1 was −22%. Each quarter of Q2-Q3 will show whether the cohort maths holds.
Capital allocation: ₹5,600 cr of treasury, the FinZ sale, Sarrthi IAS tranches and any new acquisition or school investment.
Supply: free float is under 30%; the founders' 18-month lock-in on their minimum contribution ends in May-2027.

sections.title: A low-price online test-prep platform that also runs a fast-grown offline network

blocks.p: PW prepares students for India's competitive exams: engineering (JEE), medicine (NEET), civil services (UPSC), CA, government jobs, MBA and others, plus school-level "Foundation" (grades 6-10), state boards, K-12 tuition (Curious Jr) and short skills courses. It earns in two ways. **Online** (52% of FY26 revenue on the new basis): live and recorded classes, tests and doubt-solving on its app, sold as yearly "batches" at about ₹4,000 (ACPU ₹4,104 in FY26), with add-ons (Infinity, Power Batch). **Offline** (47%): classroom courses at 366 centres (Jun-2026), at ₹36,625 of revenue per student in FY26 (about nine times the online price): Vidyapeeth (classic classrooms, ~70% of offline revenue), Pathshala (a star teacher on screen plus a local doubt teacher), category centres (UPSC, CA, defence) and three acquired regional chains (Xylem in Kerala, Utkarsh in Rajasthan, Knowledge Planet in the UAE). Its funnel is largely free: 142 million+ followers on social media, mostly YouTube (9.5 billion+ views), so advertising was only 9.1% of revenue in FY26.

blocks.callout: **Two businesses with opposite economics.** Online is a one-teacher-to-many product: the content is made once, the marginal student costs little, and margins were ~27% in FY26 after rent. Offline is a classroom business with rent, local faculty and 80-student batches; it earns 13-15% only when a centre is mature and full, and the network as a whole lost ~10% of revenue in FY26. The valuation question is how much of the group's future profit comes from each.

sections.title: From a YouTube channel (2014) to a listed company (2025) in eleven years

blocks.p: Alakh Pandey started teaching physics on YouTube in 2014; the channel had 2 million subscribers by 2019. He and Prateek Boob incorporated the company in 2020 and launched the app. Growth after that came in three waves: low-priced online batches for JEE and NEET (2020-22), offline centres from 2022 plus acquisitions of regional coaching chains (Xylem, Utkarsh, Knowledge Planet, Sarrthi IAS), and from 2025 a push into school-age learners (K-12 tuition, state boards, a school-management company). The IPO in Nov-2025 raised ₹3,100 cr of new money; the founders sold ₹380 cr and still own 71%.

blocks.callout: **Corporate actions to remember when reading the numbers:** (1) the pre-IPO bonus (35 new shares for each one held) means all per-share history is restated; (2) the preference shares were liabilities at fair value until FY24, which explains part of the FY24 loss; (3) acquisitions came with put options for the sellers' remaining stakes, carried as a redemption liability rather than debt; (4) FY26 channel revenue was restated in Q1FY27 (B2B and some "others" moved into online and offline), so old and new channel numbers do not compare directly.

sections.title: Test prep is a ₹1.1 lakh crore market growing ~13%, and only a small part of it is online

blocks.p: India spends ₹15-16 lakh crore a year on education (FY25, Redseer in AR FY26). Test preparation is ₹1.0-1.1 lakh crore (~7%), K-12 ₹7.7-8.7 lakh crore (~52%) and higher education ₹5.5-6 lakh crore. Online is only ~4% of education spending, the lowest of any big consumer category (retail 7-10%, travel 35-40%). Redseer, quoted by JPMorgan, expects test prep to grow ~13% a year over FY25-30 and online test prep ~29%. Demand rests on a hard fact: far more students sit JEE, NEET, UPSC and government-job exams than there are seats or posts, and families pay to improve the odds. Management puts the test-prep pool at ~6 crore students growing 13-15% a year (Q3FY26 call).

blocks.p: Offline JEE and NEET coaching is led by long-established chains (Allen, Aakash, FIITJEE and regional institutes in Kota, Hyderabad and Kerala), which compete on top ranks; PW competes on price and its online brand, and says it now produces the most JEE and NEET selections but still trails on top-100 ranks. Online, the venture-funded wave of 2020-22 (Byju's, Unacademy, Vedantu) shrank after the pandemic, leaving PW as the only scaled profitable online test-prep player (DAM Capital estimates ~20% share of online JEE/NEET). The next competitor may not be a coaching company at all: general AI tutors are free, which is why PW is building its own (Ask AI, AI Guru, an AI tutor in beta).

Ministry of Education guidelines for coaching centres circulated to states on 16-Jan-2024 (registration, no enrolment below 16 or before secondary-school exams, graduate tutors; advisory until states legislate; Business Today 19-Jan-2024); NEET moving online from 2027 (NTA). Coaching guidelines mainly affect offline centres (age limits, fees, space per student); they are advisory until states legislate. The NEET-UG paper was cancelled and re-held in 2026, the second disruption in three years, and NTA plans to move NEET online from 2027, which management sees as a tailwind for digital preparation.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** the sector tailwind (more students chasing scarce seats, a slow shift online) reaches PW directly in online, where it grows faster than the market at high margins and low acquisition cost. In offline it has grown mainly by opening centres, which shows up as revenue before it shows up as profit. With centre openings now slowed, offline growth will have to come from fuller centres and higher fees; that is the test for FY27-28.

sections.title: Online: ~4.9 million paying students at ~₹4,100 a year, ~27% margin after rent, growing ~30%

blocks.p: Online revenue was ₹2,011 cr in FY26 on the new basis (₹1,954 cr as first reported, +39%) and ₹549 cr in Q1FY27 (+33%). Growth is volume plus price: paying users rose 18% to 4.87 million in FY26 and collection per user rose 11% to ₹4,104 as students bought add-ons (Infinity and Infinity Pro: +32% orders in Q1FY27). The mix is broadening: JEE and NEET were 54% of online enrolments in FY23 and 29% in FY26, as Foundation, boards, UPSC, CA and state-language batches grew. Q1FY27 lost NEET money to the re-held exam (NEET online collections −28%), then made it back from July (+51% to mid-August).

blocks.p: Profitability: management grades categories in three bands. JEE, NEET, CA, MBA, commerce and boards are "high profitability"; GATE, UPSC, state PSCs, Foundation and government exams are profitable with room to improve; NEET PG, skills, Curious Jr and vernacular are still investments (Curious Jr to break even in FY27). Online pre-IndAS margin was ~27% in FY26 and 12% in seasonally weak Q1FY27 (6% a year earlier). We forecast online channel EBITDA (Ind AS basis, before ESOP) of 28.5% / 30.5% / 31.5% for FY27-29E, i.e. ~27.6-30.7% after rent, on revenue of ₹2,655 / 3,398 / 4,247 cr (32% / 28% / 25% growth).

blocks.callout: **Why online works:** one recorded or live class serves thousands, the YouTube funnel brings students for little advertising, and prices of ~₹4,000 a year are a tenth of offline coaching, so the market expands rather than just shifting. The risk is the same feature in reverse: low prices leave little room if free AI tutors set the reference price at zero.

sections.title: Offline: 366 centres, still losing money after rent; mature centres earn 13-15%

blocks.p: Offline revenue was ₹1,844 cr in FY26 (new basis; ₹1,774 cr as first reported, +31%) and ₹490 cr in Q1FY27 (+14%; 20-25% without the NEET delay, management). The network grew from 198 centres at Mar-25 to 353 at Mar-26 and 366 at Jun-26; students from 0.33 to 0.47 million. Vidyapeeth is ~70% of offline revenue. The economics depend on centre age: centres opened in 2022-24 were EBITDA-positive in FY26 (the 2023-24 cohort at 13-15%, except Kota, where student numbers have fallen), while the 2025 cohort lost a single-digit margin. Newer centres are smaller ("hyperlocal") and are meant to break even within 24 months.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** management guides offline to near break-even after rent in FY27. We are a year behind that (−5% in FY27E), as are JM Financial and DAM Capital. The levers are credible (fewer openings, fuller centres, more students per teacher, fees up 7% in Q1), but offline is a crowded, results-driven market where PW still trails the incumbents on top ranks, and every new centre restarts the two-year loss cycle.

sections.title: K-12, AI products and schools: small today, and where the capital-allocation risk sits

blocks.p: Online K-12 and early learning (Foundation, pre-Foundation, Curious Jr, commerce, boards incl. 14 state boards) earned ₹105 cr in Q1FY27, +88%, on 0.78 million enrolments (+41%); management sees state boards (~6 crore students) as the next JEE/NEET-sized category. AI products are both cost levers and new revenue: Ask AI answers most doubts, AI Guru handled 102 million queries in Q1, PW Books (AI digital books from ₹999) took 23,000 paid orders in ten days, and a one-to-one AI tutor is in beta at ~$0.20 an hour of voice tutoring. Capital-heavy bets are being scaled back: FinZ (student loans) is being sold and management says there will be no large school-running programme, after allocating ₹400 cr to a school-management company in FY26.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** PW has a moat online, built on Alakh Pandey's brand, a free YouTube funnel and the lowest price point in the market; it shows up as ~27% margins with advertising at 9% of revenue. It is a narrow moat: a student is a customer for a year or two, there are no switching costs, and the brand is tied to a few teachers. Offline has no moat: it is a local, capital-hungry business where PW is a newcomer competing with established chains on results. AI is both the biggest opportunity (cheaper teaching at scale) and the biggest threat (free substitutes).

sections.title: Revenue up 5x in three years; the first profitable year before tax came in FY26

blocks.p: Revenue went from ₹744 cr in FY23 to ₹3,900 cr in FY26 (+74% a year), with growth slowing from 161% in FY24 to 49% and 35%. The losses came from building the offline network: in FY24 the company lost ₹1,131 cr (including fair-value charges on preference shares then held as liabilities), in FY25 ₹243 cr and in FY26 only ₹24 cr, after ₹63 cr of IPO and one-off costs. Profit before tax was ₹10 cr in FY26, the first positive year. The business is seasonal: students pay in March-September, but revenue is booked over the batch, so Q2 and Q3 carry the profit and Q4 and Q1 show losses. Q1FY27 lost ₹88 cr (₹127 cr a year earlier).

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the turn to profit is real but thin. FY26 EBITDA in our model (revenue less operating costs including ₹171 cr of share-based pay, before rent is counted under Ind AS 116) was ₹370 cr, a 9.5% margin. After rent the company's own "pre-IndAS" EBITDA was ₹300 cr (7.7%), and other income of ₹232 cr on the IPO cash is what made the year profitable before tax. Operating leverage is visible (employee costs before ESOP fell from 45.4% to 44.5% of revenue, advertising from 9.6% to 9.1%), but the offline network still loses money.

sections.title: Four EBITDA numbers, upfront fees and a big ESOP bill: read the profit carefully

blocks.p: PW publishes four versions of EBITDA, and they differ by more than the profit itself. The cleanest is **pre-IndAS EBITDA**: revenue less all cash operating costs including rent, before share-based pay and other income: ₹300 cr in FY26 (7.7%). **Adjusted EBITDA** (₹784 cr) adds back rent and other income; **EBITDA** (₹549 cr) deducts ESOP and exceptional items but keeps other income. Our model (Screener basis) uses revenue less operating costs including ESOP, before rent and other income: ₹370 cr. Two further points: ESOP cost was ₹171 cr in FY26 (4.4% of revenue, up from 3.2%), a real cost paid in shares; and other income (₹232 cr, mostly interest on the IPO cash) was larger than FY26 profit before tax (₹10 cr).

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the accounting is conventional and EY-audited, but the presentation leans on flattering EBITDA definitions. We value on EBITDA after ESOP (a real cost) and treat rent as debt, which is consistent with the stock's own history. On the company's "adjusted EBITDA" the group looks twice as profitable as it is.

sections.title: Students pay upfront: ₹238 cr left in FY26 after capex and rent, and the IPO cash is mostly unspent

blocks.p: Physicswallah's cash comes before its revenue. Fees are collected at enrolment and booked over the course, so contract liabilities (fees received, not yet earned) were ₹1,149 cr at Mar-2026, up from ₹864 cr. In FY26 operating cash of ₹833 cr paid for ₹343 cr of capex (centre fit-outs, servers) and ₹252 cr of lease payments, leaving ₹238 cr. The ₹3,100 cr fresh issue (Nov-2025) was mostly unspent at Mar-2026 (₹768 cr used, of which ₹547 cr on acquisitions and general purposes, the biggest use so far). Treasury was ₹5,027 cr at Mar-2026 and ₹5,601 cr at Jun-2026, the Q1 rise being student fees paid in advance.

blocks.callout: **The capital question:** the core needs little capital, so how the ₹5,000 cr+ treasury is used decides returns. So far: an aggressive offline build (155 centres in FY26), a K-12 school-management company (₹400 cr allocated), acquisitions with put options to buy out minorities (Xylem, Utkarsh, Sarrthi IAS: up to 85% by FY31), and a lending arm (FinZ) now being sold. After investor pushback management now says capital goes to online content, AI and "selective" online acquisitions, with offline opening "opportunistic". We take that at face value but watch it.

sections.title: Treasury ₹5,027 cr at Mar-2026 against ₹1,042 cr of lease liabilities and ₹10 cr of bank debt

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 the group held ₹5,027 cr of treasury (company definition: investments ₹2,421 cr, bank and cash ₹1,126 cr, and ~₹1,475 cr of deposits in other financial assets). Bank borrowings were ₹10.5 cr; lease liabilities on centres, hostels and offices were ₹1,042 cr. Screener files two equity items as "borrowings": the preference shares at Mar-2025 (₹834 cr) and an ₹824 cr reserve at Mar-2026. We count both as equity in net worth; the borrowings line below still includes them (as Screener and our Excel model show it), and offset the ₹824 cr in the investments line, so net cash is right (PWL.patch.js). Goodwill was ₹274 cr (Xylem, Utkarsh, Sarrthi and others; ₹16 cr impaired in FY26). Other financial liabilities of ₹463 cr include the redemption liability for buying out minority shareholders of acquired companies.

sections.title: The street: 6 of 8 brokers positive; median target ₹139, mostly on EV/EBITDA by channel

blocks.p: Coverage started after the IPO quiet period (Goldman Sachs Neutral ₹135 on 24-Dec-2025; Axis Capital Add ₹138 in Jan-2026) and widened through 2026 (JM Financial, JPMorgan, HSBC, DAM Capital, Motilal Oswal, BofA). sections.title: Valuation: 28x Sep-28E EBITDA gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}; the market pays 28.6x FY28E

blocks.p: The street values PW on EV/EBITDA 1.5-2 years forward, mostly channel by channel (JM 32x online / 15x offline on Jun-28E; JPMorgan 30x / 10x; Motilal 50x / 15x on FY28E) and once for the group (HSBC 35x FY28E adjusted EBITDA). P/E is not used: profit is small and mostly interest on the IPO cash. We use EV/EBITDA on the same horizon (Sep-28E: half FY28E, half FY29E) for the group, on EBITDA after ESOP and before rent, with lease liabilities (₹1,042 cr at Mar-2026) counted as debt, the basis on which the stock's own short history can be measured. On the street's basis (EBITDA after rent, before ESOP, gross treasury) our target equals **31.4x** Sep-28E pre-IndAS EBITDA of ₹1,137 cr.

assumptions._note: Channel model (as the company now reports): Online, Offline and Others grow on revenue; channel EBITDA = channel pre-IndAS EBITDA + channel lease payments (Ind AS 116 basis, before ESOP, corporate costs allocated as the company does). Model EBITDA = channels − ESOP (Screener basis: before other income, after ESOP). Valued on EV/EBITDA on Sep-28E (roll FY28E/FY29E 50:50), the street's method; the multiple is derived in PWL.ctx.js and written by PWL.val.js. ₹ crore.

segments.name: Online
segments._why: Online revenue +39% in FY26 (old basis) and +33% in Q1FY27 despite a 28% fall in NEET collections in the quarter (the exam was re-held); collections +51% from 1-Jul to 13-Aug. K-12 and early learning +88%, ACPU +10%. We use 32% for FY27E (JM 31%), then 28% and 25% as JEE/NEET mature and the newer categories (K-12, state boards, vernacular, NEET PG) carry growth. BofA has 29% a year FY26-29, Motilal 28% FY26-30.
segments._marginWhy: Online pre-IndAS margin ~27% in FY26 (management, Q1FY27 call; Motilal and DAM ~26%), 12% in seasonally weak Q1FY27 (6% a year earlier). Adding ~1% of revenue for online lease payments gives ~28% on our basis. We assume 28.5% / 30.5% / 31.5% (pre-IndAS ~27.5% / 29.5% / 30.5%), in line with Motilal (~30% by FY28) and DAM (~31% by FY28) and below JPMorgan (33%).

segments.name: Offline (Vidyapeeth, Pathshala, other centres, Xylem, Utkarsh, Knowledge Planet)
segments._why: Offline +31% in FY26 (old basis) on 155 new centres; +14% in Q1FY27 as the NEET re-exam delayed batches (20-25% without it, management); enrolments +82% since July. Centre additions have slowed: 366 at Jun-26 against 353 at Mar-26, with new plans 'opportunistic'. We assume 24% in FY27E (JM 27.7%), then 18% and 15% as growth shifts to filling existing centres and ARPU (+7% in Q1).
segments._marginWhy: Offline pre-IndAS margin ~-19% in FY25 and ~-10% in FY26 (Q4FY26 call), -22% in seasonally weak Q1FY27 (-26% a year earlier). Guidance: near break-even in FY27; mature 2023-24 centres earn 13-15%. Lease payments are ~14% of offline revenue, so our Ind AS basis = pre-IndAS + ~13 points. We assume pre-IndAS -6% / -3% / -1% (Ind AS 6.5% / 10% / 12%): break-even a year later than guided, as JM (-2.5% in FY27E) and DAM (positive only in FY28) also doubt the FY27 target; Motilal has +3% by FY28.

segments.name: Others (ads, content licensing, FinZ, new bets)
segments._why: ₹44 cr in FY26 (new basis), ₹15 cr in Q1FY27. FinZ lending is being sold (term sheet signed, Aug-2026). Immaterial to value.
segments._marginWhy: Loss ₹5 cr in Q1FY27 (-34%); losses narrow as FinZ is exited (JM cut its Others loss estimates after Q1). -40% / -25% / -15%.

assumptions._unallocWhy: The company allocates corporate costs to the channels (₹57 cr in Q1FY27, Appendix C), so nothing is left unallocated.
assumptions._esopWhy: Share-based pay ₹171 cr in FY26 (4.4% of revenue; ₹91 cr in FY25) and ₹39 cr in Q1FY27 (flat YoY). Options at ₹1 exercise price; new grants each year. Non-cash but dilutive.
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex ₹343 cr in FY26 (centre fit-outs, servers, content) plus lease principal ₹167 cr. Centre openings slow in FY27 (plans to be set over Q2-Q3); the IPO earmarked ₹461 cr for fit-outs (₹441 cr unspent at Mar-26). We use cash capex ₹300 / 330 / 360 cr plus lease principal ₹200 / 230 / 260 cr (new right-of-use assets), so the DCF pays for rent.
assumptions._depWhy: D&A ₹437 cr in FY26 on average gross block (incl. right-of-use) of ~₹2,540 cr = 17%; Q1FY27 ₹111 cr (₹444 cr annualised). 16% gives ₹475 / 560 / 655 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Treasury ₹5,027 cr at Mar-26 and ₹5,601 cr at Jun-26 (company), earning ~6.5-7% (other income ₹232 cr in FY26 on a treasury that rose from ~₹1,400 cr to ₹5,000 cr with the Nov-2025 IPO; ₹109 cr in Q1FY27). The model earns the yield on treasury net of lease liabilities, so the fixed item adds 6.5% on the ~₹1,050-1,260 cr of lease liabilities, i.e. on the gross treasury.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Yield on the part of gross treasury that the model nets against lease liabilities (6.5% × ₹1,050 / 1,150 / 1,260 cr). No other recurring non-operating income.
assumptions._interestWhy: Finance cost ₹102 cr in FY26 (lease interest ~₹85 cr), ₹26 cr in Q1FY27. Bank debt only ₹10.5 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: Statutory ~25.2% plus losses in subsidiaries and new bets that cannot be offset (FY26 tax ₹34 cr on PBT ₹10 cr). Carried-forward losses with a deferred tax asset are small (₹51 cr).
assumptions._payoutWhy: No dividend policy; cash is kept for acquisitions, AI and centres.

otherTreasury.label: Bank deposits and other treasury in other financial assets
otherTreasury._why: Company treasury ₹5,027.25 cr at Mar-26 (AR FY26, Q4 letter: investments, other financial assets, cash and bank balances) less Screener's investments ₹2,426 cr and cash ₹1,126 cr; the difference sits in other financial assets (₹1,868 cr, mainly fixed deposits). Screener files ₹823.60 cr of equity (other equity reserve) as preference capital in borrowings; PWL.patch.js offsets it in investments, so net treasury = ₹5,027 cr less true borrowings of ₹1,052 cr (leases ₹1,041.6 cr, bank ₹10.5 cr) = ₹3,975 cr.

rentBuild._why: Lease payments (principal + interest) translate our Ind AS EBITDA into the pre-IndAS EBITDA the company and the street use. FY26 ₹252 cr (Q4FY26 letter), Q1FY27 ₹71 cr.

dcf._betaWhy: Young listed consumer-internet/edtech stock with regulatory risk: beta 1.1, cost of equity 13.1% (as Eternal and Meesho). Bank debt is nil; lease liabilities are deducted as debt, so the cost of equity is the discount rate.
dcf._tgWhy: 6%: India's test-prep and tuition market grows ~13% (Redseer via AR FY26) and online penetration is ~4%; 6% nominal after 15 years.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~20% in FY29E to 9% by year 15.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA (Ind AS, after ESOP) rises from ~20% in FY29E to 24%: online at ~31% and offline at its 13-15% mature-centre level, less ESOP of ~2.5% of revenue.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex incl. lease principal 8.4% of revenue in FY29E, fading to 7% (cash capex ~3.5%, leases ~3.5%); D&A incl. right-of-use 6.5% long run (11.2% in FY26).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: How the street values PW: EV/EBITDA 1.5-2 years forward, mostly by channel (JM 32x online / 15x offline on Jun-28E; Motilal 50x / 15x FY28E; JPMorgan 30x / 10x) or for the group (HSBC 35x FY28E adjusted EBITDA). We apply one multiple to group EBITDA (Ind AS, after ESOP, lease liabilities in net debt), the basis on which the stock's own history can be measured. Derived in PWL.ctx.js (own one-year-forward EV/EBITDA median since 1-Jan-2026 × the internet platforms' EV/EBITDA move over the same window) and written by PWL.val.js.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Own one-year-forward P/E median since 1-Jan-2026 × the same internet platforms' P/E move over the window (PWL.ctx.js); JM's ₹110 initiation implied 70x FY28 P/E.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF (lease principal treated as capex), cost of equity 13.1%, terminal growth 6%.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Online keeps growing above 30% as K-12, state boards and vernacular scale and AI products (PW Books, AI tutor) monetise; offline hits its FY27 break-even guidance and mature-centre margins spread; the market pays its own forward median with no sector de-rating.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: JEE/NEET online saturates and free AI tutors cap pricing; the offline network stays loss-making as Allen, Aakash and local players fight for seats and Kota-style demand shocks spread; growth halves to the mid-teens; the market pays the 25th percentile of its own forward multiple, with the sector move.
